subtitle: NumPy — the numerical library underneath pandas, scikit-learn, and matplotlib.

code:
import numpy as np

prices = np.array([20.0, 55.5, 130.0, 8.25])
print(prices.dtype)   # float64
print(prices.shape)   # (4,)
print(prices.ndim)    # 1
print(prices.size)    # 4
caption: Every value shares one dtype — that restriction is what makes NumPy fast.
Built from a list of lists; shape reports rows then columns.
Arrays do arithmetic element-by-element; lists just repeat with *.
The NumPy equivalent of WHERE price > 50 — the single most-used pattern in this chapter.

code:
print(np.array([1, 2.5]).dtype)          # float64
print(np.array([1.9, 2.7]).astype(int))  # [1 2]

x = np.array([1.0, np.nan, 3.0])
print(x.sum(), np.nansum(x))             # nan 4.0
caption: astype(int) truncates, not rounds. nansum ignores missing values; plain sum doesn't.
linspace includes both endpoints; reshape needs the same total element count.
